opening.text: A small child wakes up at night in a dark room. Everything looks bigger. A coat on a chair looks like a monster. Then a parent turns on the night light. The room is the same. But it doesn't feel the same anymore. Fear shrinks when the light comes on. Jesus Christ is that light.

mainMessage.text: Fear shrinks when the light comes on. The Savior is the light.

blocks.text: **Fear is old** Fear isn't a modern problem. It has been with us since the beginning.
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Fear is not new.
Fear is old.
**Name what scares you** It helps to know what is under the bed. Name the fear.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
We fear failure, rejection, disappointment, and the unknown.
Name the fear.
**Be ready, and don't be afraid** A night light doesn't remove the dark. It helps us be ready. Being prepared helps us stay calm.

I tell you these things because of your prayers; wherefore, treasure up wisdom in your bosoms, lest the wickedness of men reveal these things unto you by their wickedness, in a manner which shall speak in your ears with a voice louder than that which shall shake the earth; but if ye are prepared ye shall not fear.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Yes, we live in perilous times, but as we stay on the covenant path, we need not fear.
Be prepared.
**Choose a bold confidence** We can choose to live in the light, not in the corner of the room.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us set aside our fears and live instead with joy, humility, hope, and a bold confidence that the Lord is with us.
Set fear aside.
**Love turns on the light** When a child knows a parent is near, fear fades. Christ's love does the same for us.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Christ’s love will replace fear with faith!
Love replaces fear.
**We don't have to freeze** A scared child may freeze in bed. But we can get up. As covenant people, we don't have to be stuck.

Wherefore, be of good cheer, and do not fear, for I the Lord am with you, and will stand by you; and ye shall bear record of me, even Jesus Christ, that I am the Son of the living God, that I was, that I am, and that I am to come.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
As His covenant people, we need not be paralyzed by fear because bad things might happen.
Don't freeze.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when fear came and they found calm. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The storm on the sea

blocks.text: A storm hit the boat. The disciples were afraid. Jesus was asleep.

And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
The Savior was in the boat the whole time. He is in ours too.

application.text: First, name one fear that bothers you most. Second, pray and tell Heavenly Father about it. Third, take one small step toward the thing you fear, with Him beside you.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know the Savior is in the boat with us. I know His love is stronger than fear. I know faith can replace fear. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

invitations: I invite you to name one fear that bothers you most.
I invite you to pray and tell Heavenly Father about it.
I invite you to take one small step toward the thing you fear, with Him beside you.

closingVerse.text: God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;

opening.text: Think of the first day at a new school. The hallways are huge. The faces are strange. Your stomach is in knots. Then a teacher smiles and says, "I'm glad you're here." Suddenly it's a little easier. Fear often loosens when we know someone is with us.

mainMessage.text: Fear loosens when we know someone is with us. The Lord is with us.

blocks.text: **Everyone has a first day** Every person has felt afraid. Fear is an old companion of humankind.
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Fear is not new.
Everyone has felt it.
**What the new student fears** Will I fit in? Will I fail? What will happen? Those are common fears.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
We fear failure, rejection, disappointment, and the unknown.
These are common fears.
**Study ahead** A smart student prepares the night before. Being prepared brings calm, even in hard times.

Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Yes, we live in perilous times, but as we stay on the covenant path, we need not fear.
Prepare ahead.
**Walk in with confidence** We don't have to walk in with our shoulders down. We can walk in with hope.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us set aside our fears and live instead with joy, humility, hope, and a bold confidence that the Lord is with us.
Walk in with hope.
**A teacher who cares** A caring teacher makes the room feel safe. Christ's love makes our world feel safe in the same way.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Christ’s love will replace fear with faith!
Love makes it safe.
**Don't be frozen at the door** Some students stand at the door and never go in. Don't be paralyzed. Walk in.

Wherefore, be of good cheer, and do not fear, for I the Lord am with you, and will stand by you; and ye shall bear record of me, even Jesus Christ, that I am the Son of the living God, that I was, that I am, and that I am to come.

Walk in.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they did something new even though they were afraid. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Elisha's servant sees the army

blocks.text: An army surrounded the city. Elisha's young servant panicked.

And when the servant of the man of God was risen early, and gone forth, behold, an host compassed the city both with horses and chariots. And his servant said unto him, Alas, my master! how shall we do? And he answered, Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them. And Elisha prayed, and said, Lord, I pray thee, open his eyes, that he may see. And the Lord opened the eyes of the young man; and he saw: and, behold, the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha.
The servant saw only danger. Then his eyes were opened. Heavenly help was already there.

application.text: First, think of a place where you feel afraid to go or speak. Second, ask Heavenly Father to open your eyes to the help around you. Third, walk in anyway.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know there are more with us than against us. I know the Lord goes before us. I know courage follows when we take the first step. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

closingVerse.text: Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the Lord thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

opening.text: A smoke alarm is a good thing. When there's a fire, it wakes you up. But if it goes off every time you make toast, you get tired of it. Some fear is a useful alarm. Some fear is just noise. The trick is to know which is which, and to not let the noise run your life.

mainMessage.text: Some fear is a useful alarm. Much of it is only noise. Faith helps us tell the difference.

blocks.text: **Alarms are old** Fear has been going off since the beginning. It isn't a sign that something is wrong with us.
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Fear is not new.
The alarm is old.
**What sets it off** Most alarms are set off by the same few things. Failure. Rejection. Disappointment. The unknown.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
We fear failure, rejection, disappointment, and the unknown.
Know what sets it off.
**A working alarm is a prepared one** A house with working alarms and a plan is safer. Prepared people stay calmer.

I tell you these things because of your prayers; wherefore, treasure up wisdom in your bosoms, lest the wickedness of men reveal these things unto you by their wickedness, in a manner which shall speak in your ears with a voice louder than that which shall shake the earth; but if ye are prepared ye shall not fear.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Yes, we live in perilous times, but as we stay on the covenant path, we need not fear.
Be prepared.
**Turn down the noise** When the alarm is false, we can turn it down. We can choose joy and confidence instead.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us set aside our fears and live instead with joy, humility, hope, and a bold confidence that the Lord is with us.
Turn down the noise.
**A better signal** There's a stronger signal than fear. It is Christ's love, and it brings faith.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Christ’s love will replace fear with faith!
Love is the better signal.
**Act, don't freeze** An alarm is meant to get us moving, not frozen. We move forward with the Lord beside us.

Wherefore, be of good cheer, and do not fear, for I the Lord am with you, and will stand by you; and ye shall bear record of me, even Jesus Christ, that I am the Son of the living God, that I was, that I am, and that I am to come.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
As His covenant people, we need not be paralyzed by fear because bad things might happen.
Move, don't freeze.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when fear was a warning, or when it was only noise. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Moses at the Red Sea

blocks.text: The army of Egypt was behind Israel. The sea was ahead.

And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace. And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and the Lord caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.
The people were trapped. They had every reason for alarm. But the Lord opened a way they couldn't have seen.

application.text: First, list your top two fears. Second, ask yourself, "Is this a real warning, or just noise?" Third, act on the real ones, and give the rest to the Lord in prayer.

closingVerse.text: Verily I say unto you my friends, fear not, let your hearts be comforted; yea, rejoice evermore, and in everything give thanks;

opening.text: Stand at the edge of a cold lake. Your toes touch the water and you pull back. Too cold. You stand there thinking about it. The longer you wait, the colder it feels. Then someone jumps in and says, "It's fine once you're in." Fear is often loudest at the edge. In the water, it gets quieter.

mainMessage.text: Fear is loudest at the edge. Once we step in, it grows quiet.

blocks.text: **Everyone has stood there** Everyone has stood at the edge of the water. Fear is nothing new.
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Fear is not new.
Everyone has stood there.
**What keeps us on the shore** Fear of failing. Fear of what people will think. Fear of what we can't see.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.

We fear failure, rejection, disappointment, and the unknown.

I tell you these things because of your prayers; wherefore, treasure up wisdom in your bosoms, lest the wickedness of men reveal these things unto you by their wickedness, in a manner which shall speak in your ears with a voice louder than that which shall shake the earth; but if ye are prepared ye shall not fear.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Yes, we live in perilous times, but as we stay on the covenant path, we need not fear.
Know the lake.
**Step in with confidence** We don't have to inch in with dread. We can step in with hope.
For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us set aside our fears and live instead with joy, humility, hope, and a bold confidence that the Lord is with us.

**The water is kinder than it looked** Often the thing we feared is gentler than we thought. Love and faith do their work.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).

Faith replaces fear.
**Don't be frozen on the dock** Some people stay at the edge all summer. We don't have to. We can move.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they stepped in despite fear. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Daniel in the lions’ den

blocks.text: Daniel knew the king's order. He prayed anyway, as he always had.

Now when Daniel knew that the writing was signed, he went into his house; and his windows being open in his chamber toward Jerusalem, he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime. My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions’ mouths, that they have not hurt me: forasmuch as before him innocency was found in me; and also before thee, O king, have I done no hurt.
Daniel didn't change his habit out of fear. He kept praying. And God kept him safe.

opening.text: A small child crossing a busy street holds a parent's hand. The cars are loud. The street is wide. The child is still a little scared. But the hand is strong, and the child walks. Fear and trust can sit side by side. We can be afraid and still cross, because someone holds our hand.

mainMessage.text: We can feel afraid and still cross, because the Lord holds our hand.

blocks.text: **All children feel it** No child crosses the street without feeling something. Fear has been part of life from the start.
And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Fear is not new.
All feel it.
**What the child sees** Big cars. Fast traffic. The other side far away. We have our own versions of these.
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
We fear failure, rejection, disappointment, and the unknown.
See it honestly.
**Look both ways** A parent teaches the child to look both ways. Preparation is part of crossing safely.

I tell you these things because of your prayers; wherefore, treasure up wisdom in your bosoms, lest the wickedness of men reveal these things unto you by their wickedness, in a manner which shall speak in your ears with a voice louder than that which shall shake the earth; but if ye are prepared ye shall not fear.
Elder Ronald A. Rasband of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Be Not Troubled” from the October 2018 general conference (Saturday Morning Session).
Yes, we live in perilous times, but as we stay on the covenant path, we need not fear.
Look both ways.

For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Let us set aside our fears and live instead with joy, humility, hope, and a bold confidence that the Lord is with us.
Walk with confidence.
**The hand that holds us** The child isn't afraid of the hand. The hand is love. Christ's love holds us, and fear gives way to faith.
There is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
Christ’s love will replace fear with faith!
Hold the hand.
**Don't stand frozen at the curb** A child who refuses to cross never reaches the other side. We don't have to be stuck.

Wherefore, be of good cheer, and do not fear, for I the Lord am with you, and will stand by you; and ye shall bear record of me, even Jesus Christ, that I am the Son of the living God, that I was, that I am, and that I am to come.
President Dieter F. Uchtdorf, Second Counselor in the First Presidency, said this in his talk “Perfect Love Casteth Out Fear” from the April 2017 general conference (Sunday Morning Session).
As His covenant people, we need not be paralyzed by fear because bad things might happen.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone held their hand through a scary moment. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The women at the empty tomb

blocks.text: Two women came to the tomb early. They were afraid. An angel spoke to them, and then the Savior did.

And the angel answered and said unto the women, Fear not ye: for I know that ye seek Jesus, which was crucified. Then said Jesus unto them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they go into Galilee, and there shall they see me.
They were afraid, and they were told to go anyway. They went. They met the risen Lord.
